effects.text: Pick-time choice: increase one skill modifier by 5.
Pick-time choice: increase one skill modifier by 2.
Melee weapon attacks that deal bludgeoning damage, and unarmed attacks, deal one additional damage die. Unarmed and melee weapon attacks cost 1 more AP.
Melee weapon attacks that deal bludgeoning damage, and unarmed attacks, deal +3 damage. Unarmed and melee weapon attacks cost 2 more AP.
Damage you deal with a weapon is increased by 1. When you roll a 1 on an attack roll, the weapon gains two levels of decay instead of one.
Damage you deal with a weapon is increased by 2. Whenever you attack with a weapon, it gains Breakable.
An addicted condition ends after you rest for at least 8 hours. Disadvantage on Endurance checks to resist becoming addicted.
An addicted condition ends after 1 hour. You always become addicted after using a Chem or Robot Overclock Program.
While outside, Party Nerve effects are doubled (combat sequence temporary stamina and death save bonus). While indoors, underground or otherwise not outside, you gain no benefit from Party Nerve.
Advantage on all ability and skill checks while outside; disadvantage on all ability and skill checks while indoors, underground or otherwise not outside.
Add a d4 to any ability or skill check made from 6am to 12pm. Gain an additional level of fatigue when you fail an Endurance check to resist sleep.
+2 to all skills in the morning (6am to 12pm), -1 at night (6pm to 6am).
Advantage on Endurance checks to resist becoming addicted. Chem and Robot Overclock Program benefits last half as long as listed.
Immune to the addicted condition. Chem and Robot Overclock Program benefits last at most one round.
When spending AP to attack with a ranged weapon or explosive, you may take disadvantage on the attack roll to make it cost 1 less AP (minimum 3).
Everything from the base trait applies (ranged and explosive attacks may take disadvantage for 1 less AP, minimum 3). You cannot make targeted attacks with ranged weapons.
Melee and unarmed attacks deal an extra 2 damage. You gain no benefit from Party Nerve.

Melee and unarmed attacks deal an extra 2 damage. You gain no benefit from Party Nerve. Whenever you spend at least 6 AP to move, you immediately gain 2 AP. Disadvantage on all Barter and Speech skill checks. For perk requirements you count as having 4 Charisma.
A critical hit with a weapon increases either the damage multiplier or the damage dice by 1. Attack roll totals are reduced by 1.
A critical hit with a weapon increases either the damage multiplier or the damage dice by 2. Attack roll totals are reduced by 2.
Use Discount an additional time per rest.
Use Discount two additional times per rest.
While your SP is 0 you may gain 1 additional AP at the start of your turn; if you do, AC and DT are each decreased by 2.
While your SP is 0 you may gain 2 additional AP at the start of your turn; if you do, you do not subtract DT from damage dealt to HP and your AC is 8.
For Charisma perk requirements you count as having 2 more Charisma. For Agility and Strength perk requirements you count as having 2 less.
For Charisma perk requirements you count as having 10 Charisma. For Agility and Strength perk requirements you count as having 4.
Doubled bonus and penalty: the wording "in addition to this trait's effects" is read as stacking on the base effects.
Disadvantage on all ability checks, skill checks and attack rolls while carrying less than 50 load of weapons, armor, ammunition, explosives, chems, food, drink or junk.
You gain a level of fatigue whenever your Carry Load is below your maximum.
While your SP is 0: reroll a 1 or 2 on a weapon damage die (keep the new roll), and subtract 2 from attack rolls.
While your SP is 0: reroll a 1 or 2 on a weapon damage die (keep the new roll), subtract 2 from attack rolls, and attack damage is increased by 5. Disadvantage on all attack rolls while your SP is 0.
The chance to automatically miss (and the weapon to gain a level of decay) on any creature's attack roll is increased by 1. If your karma cap is flipped you may flip it back.
The chance for any creature's attack roll to automatically miss is increased by 2.
Throwing an explosive costs 1 less AP (minimum 3). You can throw them only up to half their listed range.
Throwing an explosive costs 1 less AP (minimum 3) and only up to half the listed range. If a thrown explosive damages another PC's HP, the damage is doubled for all non-PC creatures.
Add a d4 to any ability or skill check made from 6pm to 6am. Gain an additional level of fatigue when you fail an Endurance check to resist sleep.
-1 to all skills in the morning (6am to 12pm), +2 at night (6pm to 6am).
+2 to attack rolls with one-handed weapons; -2 to attack rolls with two-handed weapons.
+2 to damage with one-handed weapon attacks; -2 to damage with two-handed weapon attacks.
On a critical hit with a weapon, roll a d20: on a 20 the hit automatically lands and the weapon table's extra damage is quadrupled; otherwise it hits but deals no critical damage.
On a critical hit with a weapon, roll a d20; on a 20 roll another d20; on a second 20 the hit automatically lands and the weapon table's extra damage is octupled.
Doubled bonus and penalty: the wording "in addition to this trait's effects" is read as stacking on the base effects.
The extra AP cost of targeted ranged attack rolls is reduced by 1.
The extra AP cost of targeted ranged attack rolls is reduced by 2.
Whenever you succeed a radiation check, your Radiation DC increases by 4 instead of 2.

You can heal the full amount from stimpaks and can use healing powder. You are no longer immune to radiation and its effects: this cancels the Ghoul Evolution immunities, which the engine cannot remove, so ignore them.
Also has the base trait's effects (full stimpak healing, healing powder, no radiation immunity). Whenever you succeed a Radiation check, your Radiation DC increases by 4 instead of 2.
Whenever you regain stamina points from sleep, you regain half as much.

After an 8+ hour rest, roll a d20 (Sight roll) and record it. Once per rest, replace any attack roll, skill check or ability check made by you or a creature you can see with it. You start each game with one Karma Cap flipped.
Two Sight rolls after an 8+ hour rest. Your Karma Caps no longer flip if you roll a 1 on a d20.
When you restore hit points to another creature with a first aid kit, stimpak, perk or ability, restore 1 additional point. Damage you deal to another creature is reduced by 1 (minimum 1).

Also has the base trait's effects. Spending 6 AP on a Medicine check to return a dying creature to 1 hit point automatically succeeds. If an attack of yours kills a creature, you lose all abilities from this trait.
In a settlement, town, outpost or other populated location: advantage on Sneak and Breach checks, disadvantage on Speech and Barter checks.
Also has the base trait's effects. You can use Discount three times before resting. There is a bounty of over 500 caps on you (work out the details with your GM).

When you rest with other player characters, you and each other resting PC gain temporary stamina points equal to your Charisma score. Group stealth is reduced by 2 while you are within 500 feet of them.
Temporary stamina points gained are double your Charisma score. Party group stealth is reduced by 5 while you are in the party.
Advantage on Endurance checks to resist a level of Hunger or Fatigue. You fall unconscious at 8 levels of Hunger or Fatigue instead of 10.
Also has the base trait's effects. The negative effects from levels of Hunger and Fatigue are doubled. The +1 HP and +1 SP apply at each level-up that grants HP/SP (levels 3, 5, ...).
In combat sequence, your placement goes before the previous non-player creature in the turn order, regardless of their roll.
In combat sequence, your placement goes before the previous two non-player creatures in the turn order, regardless of their roll.
Pick-time choice: instead of a 1st-level perk, five different skill modifiers of your choice increase by 2.
When you flip a Karma Cap to re-roll a Skill check, make the roll at advantage. Your Karma Caps no longer flip back over when you roll a 1 on a d20.
When you flip a Karma Cap to reroll an Ability check, Skill check or attack roll, make the roll at advantage. You start each game with one Karma Cap flipped.
You gain an additional level of fatigue when you fail an Endurance check to resist sleep. The +1 SP applies at each level-up that grants SP (levels 3, 5, ...).
Also has the base trait's effects (total of 2 extra SP per level-up). When you regain stamina from any rest that isn't sleep, you regain a fourth of your maximum stamina instead of half.
The first level of decay your weapons and armor gain is ignored while they have no decay. They become non-functional at 8 levels of decay instead of 10.
The negative effects of one or two levels of decay on your weapons and armor are ignored. They become non-functional at 5 levels of decay instead of 10.
The percentage of caps off from Discount is tripled. All items cost 10% more for you.
The percentage of caps off from Discount is sextupled. All items cost 25% more for you.
When you roll combat sequence, each other player character gains advantage on their first attack roll on their turn. If a PC critically hits on that first attack, they deal no extra damage.
When you roll combat sequence, each other player character gains advantage on their first two attack rolls on their turn. Critical hits on those attacks deal no extra damage.

Travelling at a fast pace, you and other PCs move 2 additional miles per hour. At the end of each hour, each of you must succeed a DC 12 Endurance check or gain a level of fatigue; the DC increases by 2 for each PC who succeeds.
Travelling at a fast pace, you and other PCs move 5 additional miles per hour. At the end of each hour, each of you gains a level of fatigue.
A Death Save of 19 or 20 returns you to 1 hit point. You do not add your Luck or Endurance to death saves (the deathSave stat does not model this removal; ignore its LCK/END part).
A Death Save of 18, 19 or 20 returns you to 1 hit point. You do not add Luck, Endurance or Party Nerve to death saves (the deathSave stat does not model this removal).
Attack damage against a creature type you have fought before is increased by 2; against a type you haven't fought before it is decreased by 2.

Also has the base trait's effects. After combat sequence with a creature you've never rolled with before, you gain an additional 20% bonus XP on rest; for creatures you have rolled with before, you gain 10% less XP.
When you roll combat sequence, you may learn the HP, SP, AP, AC or DT total of any hostile creature; each creature you choose this for can re-roll its combat sequence.
When you roll combat sequence, you may learn two of HP, SP, AP, AC or DT of any hostile creature; each such creature can re-roll its combat sequence twice.
A 1 on an attack roll no longer automatically misses; add your modifier. Your Karma Cap does not flip back over when you roll a 1 on attack rolls.
When an attack roll is a 1, you can re-roll but must take the new result. A critical hit automatically hits but deals no extra damage.
When you sell an item you can use Discount to gain a bonus of caps equal to double your Barter skill modifier. You sell all items for 10% less than their listed value.
When you sell an item you can use Discount to gain a bonus of caps equal to triple your Barter skill modifier. You sell all items for 20% less than their listed value.
Pick-time choice: five different skill modifiers of your choice decrease by 2.
Advantage on Luck ability checks to search for items. Weapons and armor you find have one additional level of decay.
Advantage on Luck ability checks to search for items, and you can re-roll one of the dice. Weapons and armor you find have two additional levels of decay.
